subject: Cmdstan 2.9.0 gives an error, while Rstan 2.9.0 works for simple multiple dosing setting?

messages.author: 25ce5e85187da1a3
messages.subject: Cmdstan 2.9.0 gives an error, while Rstan 2.9.0 works for simple multiple dosing setting?
parts:
Hi everyone,

I am trying to implement different dosing settings with the ODE solver "integrate_ode" function in Stan. My main aim is implementing the same settings with new function "integrate_ode_cvode" as explained here: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!msg/stan-users/AkzvXZPSv6M/jcfEKozhAAAJ 

When I have a simple multiple dosing model with a first order ODE using "integrate_ode" function as described here  (https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/stan-users/uIPVPj56jdM), Rstan is working and giving reasonable results. However, Cmdstan gives an error which I attached. So, I dont know why this is happening, maybe this is a bug?

I attached the Stan model, R-code used for Rstan implemation, dump data format used for cmdstan implementation, and cmdstan error.

I am using cmdstan 2.9.0.

My sessionInfo()

Platform: x86_64-w64-mingw32/x64 (64-bit)
Running under: Windows 7 x64 (build 7601) Service Pack 1

[5] LC_TIME=German_Switzerland.1252

loaded via a namespace (and not attached):
 [1] labeling_0.3     colorspace_1.2-6 scales_0.4.0     plyr_1.8.3       tools_3.2.4     
 [6] inline_0.3.14    gtable_0.2.0     gridExtra_2.2.1  Rcpp_0.12.4      codetools_0.2-14
[11] grid_3.2.4       digest_0.6.9     stats4_3.2.4     munsell_0.4.3   


By the way, I also tried cmdstan development version by using "integrate_ode" and "integrate_ode_cvode" functions, and both gave the exactly same error.

Thank you very much for your help in advance,

Burak Kursad Gunhan

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: ODEs behave differently in CmdStan and RStan
parts:
[retitled]

The problem's that it can't evaluate the density for the first
iteration without error. It's specifically telling you (by reporting
line number) that this line is going wrong:

y_res <- integrate_ode(ode1, y_ini, tsm[1, N_t_dose]- 0.0000001, tsm[2], ke, x_r, x_i);

and specifically ahs too large an initial time. So you want to check
that tsm[1, N_t_dose] - 0.0000001 is correct in your inputs.

I retitled so that someone more familiar with the ODE errors than
me would see this and mayve have an idea what's going on. It is
possible CmdStan and RStan vary in their ODE solver at this point
because it's been under construction.

- Bob

P.S. Does your ODE have an analytic solution? If so, that'd
be a lot faster to fit.

Hi Bob,

Thank you for your response. 

Exactly, you are right that the problem is the "tsm" object, now when I change it to the same format as in Rstan, the cmdstan worked. (I attached the correct data format). Now I realize that I did not fully understand array structures in dump format.

Also, I have the analytic solution, but my main aim is extending this model to solve more complicated situations where I dont have an analytic format.

Thank you for solving the issue and regards,

Burak
